title: Thin-Cr Interference Absorber with Fixed 14-Layer Topology
scientific_hypothesis: A Cr layer constrained to 5-30 nm thickness, positioned early in a dielectric stack on Al substrate, will enable visible-band absorption through metallic loss while dielectric interference maintains high near-IR reflection.
design_principle: Thin semi-transparent metal layers absorb via their extinction coefficient while allowing sufficient transmission for dielectric interference to shape the spectral response. Quarter-wave dielectric pairs create constructive interference for reflection in the IR band.
proposed_topology: air | hfo2 | sio2 | cr | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | al
theory_basis: Recalled: thin metal films (10-50 nm) exhibit partial transmission enabling interference effects while contributing absorption through k
Recalled: quarter-wave optical thickness (n*d = lambda/4) creates high-reflection bands in dielectric stacks
Recalled: placing absorbing layer near the front of stack maximizes interaction with incident field before reflection
Recalled: Al substrate provides high baseline IR reflection that dielectric stack can enhance
expected_advantages: Cr thickness constraint forces exploration of semi-transparent regime rather than opaque blocking
Increased mutation variance on Cr layer accelerates escape from local optima
Fixed topology isolates thickness tuning as the only variable axis
known_risks: Uncertain whether 5-30 nm Cr provides sufficient absorption for visible band - may need lookup of Cr extinction coefficient spectrum
Uncertain optimal position of Cr layer in stack - index 2 is a hypothesis from recalled absorber designs
Quarter-wave estimates for dielectrics may not align with dual-band objective - actual optimal thickness may deviate significantly
No literature validation that this specific material combination achieves the stated spectral split
execution_request_english: Optimize a 14-layer planar multilayer stack with sequence: air incident, then hfo2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), Cr (Rakic-LD), hfo2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), hfo2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), hfo2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), hfo2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), hfo2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), on Al (Rakic-LD) substrate. All 14 layer thicknesses are tunable variables. Initialize Cr (Rakic-LD) layer (index 2) thickness with uniform random draws in 5-30 nm range. Initialize all dielectric layers near quarter-wave estimates (50-300 nm range). Apply 2x step-size multiplier or increased mutation variance to Cr (Rakic-LD) layer during first 5 optimization iterations. Illumination: normal incidence, unpolarized, wavelength range 400-2000 nm. Objectives: maximize mean absorptance in 400-700 nm band, maximize mean reflectance in 700-2000 nm band. Total layer count fixed at 14. Use coherent transfer matrix method solver.
revision_reason: Round 2 initialization modification: Cr layer constrained to 5-30 nm with enhanced mutation to escape high-absorption plateau
